Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(2) and the tariff shift rule in 102.21(e)(1) for headings 5508-5511, origin is conferred by a change from any heading outside that group, provided the spinning of all fibers occurs in a single country. Since the staple fibers are spun into yarn entirely in Sri Lanka (dyeing and winding are minor processes), origin is Sri Lanka.
decisive_step: Spinning the nylon staple fiber into yarn in Sri Lanka

reasoning: The track suits of HTSUS 6211.43 are not wholly obtained in a single country under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(1). Under (c)(2) and 102.21(e)(1) for headings 6210-6212, if a good consists of two or more component parts, origin is conferred by a change from unassembled components provided the good is wholly assembled in a single country. The garments are cut and wholly assembled in Guatemala. Washing, pressing, and packing in Morocco are minor processes that do not confer origin.
decisive_step: Cutting the fabric and wholly sewing and assembling the garments in Guatemala

reasoning: The anorak is not wholly obtained in a single country, excluding (c)(1). Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(2) and (e)(1), the tariff shift rule for heading 6201 (when the good consists of two or more component parts) requires a change from any other chapter, provided the good is wholly assembled in a single country. Because the cut and embroidered fabric pieces (heading 6217) fail the chapter shift, or alternatively under (c)(3), Nicaragua confers origin as the single country where the garment is wholly assembled.
decisive_step: Sewing all cut components together into the finished garment in Nicaragua

reasoning: Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(1), the blanket is not wholly obtained or produced in a single country. Moving to 19 CFR 102.21(c)(2), the tariff shift rule in 102.21(e)(1) for heading 6301 states that the country of origin is the country in which the fabric comprising the good was formed by a fabric-making process. Consistent with ruling N348858, because the polyester fabric is formed in Malaysia, Malaysia is the country of origin regardless of cutting, hemming, or packing elsewhere.
decisive_step: forming the polyester fabric in Malaysia

reasoning: The garment is not wholly obtained in a single country under 102.21(c)(1). Under 102.21(c)(2) and (e)(1), for goods of headings 6201–6208 consisting of two or more component parts, the required tariff shift is a change to an assembled good from unassembled components, provided the good is wholly assembled in a single country (see N345193). Because the cut components from China are wholly sewn together into the finished nightwear in Taiwan, Taiwan confers origin.
decisive_step: Wholly sewing the unassembled component parts into the finished garment in Taiwan

reasoning: Under 19 CFR 102.21(c)(2) and (e)(1), for cotton bed linen of subheading 6302.21, origin is conferred where the fabric is formed by a fabric-making process. Subheading 6302.21 is excluded from the dyeing and printing rule in 102.21(e)(2) because it is of cotton (see N357002). Since Italian yarn is exported to Sri Lanka where it is formed into fabric, printed, cut, and sewn into bed linen, the fabric-making process occurs in Sri Lanka, conferring Sri Lankan origin.
decisive_step: Weaving the cotton yarn into fabric in Sri Lanka
